newsitem.title: JAPAN: Aoki says its business performance is favourable.
newsitem.headline: Aoki says its business performance is favourable.

text.p: Medium-sized Japanese construction firm Aoki Corp said on Friday that its business performance has been favourable.
Aoki president Yoichiro Yano also said in a statement that the company has received broad financial support from the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) and Asahi Bank Ltd.
The construction firm's shares have fallen sharply in recent trading sessions, slipping below the 100 yen threshold for the first time on Friday.
They dipped to 64 yen at one point on Friday morning, but managed to edge up ahead of the close to end at 84 yen, down 16 yen from Thursday.
Turnover ballooned to 23.95 million yen, making it the most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.

Brokers said that jitters over the health of general contractors, burdened with problem loans from the "bubble" economy days of the late 1980s, have been rekindled since Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd applied for court protection from creditors late last week.
Aoki also said earlier on Friday that it has already put aside loan-loss reserves for loans it has guaranteed which carry a risk of default.
A company spokesman said debts on which the company had provided guarantees totalled 285.2 billion yen as of March 31, 1997, compared with 289.0 billion yen a year earlier.
The debts are held by Aoki affiliates and other firms involved in the contractor's real-estate development projects.
"We have already increased reserves for guaranteed loans with possible risks," said the spokesman.
